304:
** ἀναβαθ-μός**, ὁ,
**flight of steps, stair,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.125, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Oeconomica” 1347a5, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 65.21; δι᾽ ἀναβαθμῶν}}**by degrees,** {{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 2.557.}}
317:
Included with: ** ἀναγκ-αστός**, ή, όν,
**forced, constrained,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.58; ἀ. στρατεύοντες 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.58, compare 8.24; ἀ. τροφή 2nd c.AD: Aristides Rhetor “Orationes” 47 (23). 59}}. _adverb_ **-τῶς**{{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Axiochus” 366a}}; opposed to ἑκουσίως, {{NT|NT.1Pet.5.2.}}
326:
** ἀναζάω**,
_infinitive_ -ζῆν, **return to life, be alive again,** {{NT|NT.Luke.15.24 and 32, Sotionp.183 W.}}: in _Epic dialect_ form **ἀναερτ-ζώω** {{Refs 2nd c.BC+|2nd c.BC: Nicander Epicus “fragment” 70.5.}}
333:
** ἀναθεωρ-έω**,
**examine carefully,** {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 8.6.2, 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 12.15 (_passive_)}}; **consider a second time,** {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 1.5.1.}}
340:
** ἀνακαιν-ίζω**,
**renew,** τὸν πόλεμον{{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Marcellus” 6, compare 2nd c.AD: Appianus Historicus “Μιθριδάτειος” 37: οἶκον 6th c.AD: Hesychius Milesius Historicus 4.33}}; **revive** legend, {{NT+1st c.BC+|1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 2.1.9: _metaphorically_, ἀ. εἰς μετάνοιαν NT.Heb.6.6}}:—_passive_, τῆς ἔχθρας ἀνακεκαινισμένης{{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 7.8; ὑποθέσεις 6th c.AD: Justinianus Imperator “Novellae” 111.1.}}
341:
** ἀνακαιν-όω**,
in _passive_, **to be renewed,** {{NT|NT.2Cor.4.16, “Col.” 3.10}}:—in _middle_, **renew,** {{Refs|Heliodorus Philosophus “in Ethica Nicomachea paraphrasis - Comm. in Arist. Graeca” 221.13.}}
346:
** ἀνακεφαλαι-όομαι**,
**sum up the argument,** of an orator, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Lysia” 9; ἀ. πρὸς ἀνάμνησιν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Fragmenta” 133}}:—_passive_, **to be summed up,** ἐν τῷ λόγῳ τούτῳ{{NT|NT.Rom.13.9.}}
367:
**Ἀνανίας** (WH, Ἁναν-), -α, ὁ (Heb. חֲנַנְיָה),
**Ananias**;
1. **of Jerusalem**: Act.5:1, 3 5:5.
2. **Of Damascus**: Act.9:10-13, 17 22:12.
3. **High Priest**: Act.23:2 24:1.†
(From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)
368:
** ἀναντί-ρρητος**, ον,
**not to be opposed,** {{Refs 2nd c.BC+|2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 6.7.7, 28.13.4}}; **undeniable,** {{NT+2nd c.AD+|NT.Acts.19.36; λόγοι 2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “adversus Mathematicos” 8.160}}. _adverb_ **-τως** **without opposition, by consent,** {{Refs 2nd c.BC+|2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 22.8.11}}; **incontrovertibly**, {{Refs 6th c.AD+|“OGI” 335.138 (Pergam.), 6th c.AD: Aëtius Medicus 15.15}}; **without gainsaying,** {{NT|NT.Acts.10.29.}}
369:
Included with: ** ἀναντί-ρρητος**, ον,
**not to be opposed,** {{Refs 2nd c.BC+|2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 6.7.7, 28.13.4}}; **undeniable,** {{NT+2nd c.AD+|NT.Acts.19.36; λόγοι 2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “adversus Mathematicos” 8.160}}. _adverb_ **-τως** **without opposition, by consent,** {{Refs 2nd c.BC+|2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 22.8.11}}; **incontrovertibly**, {{Refs 6th c.AD+|“OGI” 335.138 (Pergam.), 6th c.AD: Aëtius Medicus 15.15}}; **without gainsaying,** {{NT|NT.Acts.10.29.}}
376:
** ἀνάπηρ-ος**, ον,
**maimed, mutilated,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Hermippus Comicus 35, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 24.13, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Crito” 53a, etc.; ψυχὴ ἀ. πρὸς ἀλήθειαν [prev. author] “R.” 535d; ἀνάπηρα θύειν [prev. author] Alcaeus2.149a, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Partibus Animalium” 773a13, +others}} _adverb_ **-ρως**{{NT+5th c.BC+|12th c.AD: Zonaras Legal icographus (Sts. spelt ἀνάπειρος in codices, LXX.Tob.14.2, NT.Luke.14.13, 21, compare 2nd c.AD: Phrynichus Atticista “Praeparatio Sophistica” p.13 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus)}}
379:
** ἀναπο-λόγητος**, ον,
**inexcusable,** {{NT+2nd c.BC+|2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 12.21.10, NT.Rom.1.20, 2.1}}; **undefended,** τινὰ ἐάσειν{{Refs 5th c.BC+|1st-2nd c.AD: Dio Chrysostomus Sophista 2.39, compare 4th-5th c.AD: Eunapius Historicus “Vitae Sophistarum” p.489 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus}}; **without making a defence,** {{Refs 1st c.BC+|1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 7.46.}}
387:
** ἀναστᾰτ-όω**,
**unsettle, upset,** [τὴν γῆν] {{LXX+NT|LXX.Dan.7.23; τὴν οἰκουμένην NT.Act.17.6, compare 21.38, “PMag.Par.” 1.2244}}; of the mind, {{NT|NT.Gal.5.12}}; ἀναστατοῖ με he **upsets** me, {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|“POxy.” 119.10 (2nd-3rd c.AD)}}; **destroy,** [{{Refs 2nd c.AD+|{ca. 2nd c.AD}: Aspasius Philosophus “in Ethica Nicomachea commentaria - pars” 61.28}}]; **drive out**, {{Refs 1st c.AD+|“BGU” 1079.20 (1st c.AD)}}:—_passive_, ἀναστατωθῆναι[{{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st-2nd c.AD: Harpocratio Grammaticus see {ἀνεσκευάσατο}}}]: ἀναστατοῦ ἐς τὰ ὄρη{{LXX+2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Aquila LXX.Psa.10(11).1.}}
392:
** ἀνατάσσω**,
_Attic dialect_ **ἀνα-τάττω**, _aorist 2_ _passive_ ἀνετάγην, **countermand** expenditure, {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 78.18 (_passive_)}}:—_middle_, **go regularly through again, rehearse,** {{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.968c}}; **set in order,** διήγησιν{{NT|NT.Luke.1.1.}}
